threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still hesitate at the bus stop when the 'Buses are on diversion' sign pops up, while the locals know to just wing it through the back streets.
Sat on the N35, watched a guy in a full suit try to impress a girl with his chess skills using an app. She looked baffled but amused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I truly belonged when I saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift soccer field in the middle of the street, using trash cans as goals.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can literally smell the spices from the Turkish market at Maybachufer, blending with the scent of fresh rain on cobblestones. Unique ambiance.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a native by how they expertly navigate the chaos of a Civic Center BART delay, while the newbies stand clueless in the rain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 Fulton today and a guy was giving a violin concert on the back seat. Not a single person was annoyed—only smiles all around.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about the hip bars. They miss the quiet mornings when locals gather for a simple ‘boca’ in the bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they still stare in awe at the mosaic benches in Park Güell, fumbling with their phones instead of simply enjoying the view.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'travel pass' instead of 'oyster' and think the bus is just a way to get from A to B, not a social hub.
Last night on the 35, a lad offered his sandwich to an old man. Turns out it was a full chicken bagel! The old chap just smiled, no words needed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I was sipping coffee at my favorite spot when a dog casually strolled by wearing a tiny beret. Only in Neukölln would that feel completely normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you'll find spontaneous dance parties in the U-Bahn stations during strike days. It's the city's way of turning chaos into community.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice a local will hold the door for a crowd at BART even if it's about to close; a worker will just let it slam behind them.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The delay today because of a dog on the tracks was just the cherry on top of a week of Muni chaos. Only in SF do pets derail the commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell, but miss the hidden gems like Jardins de la Vil·la Cecília—where locals actually relax away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by the way they struggle with the T-10 card machines—still scanning like it’s a self-checkout in the UK.
